RMF Reference Guide

NRAR Risk Management Framework · May 2026 · Approved by Chief Regulatory Officer

Risk Rating Scale

Bands set by 5×5 cell lookup (RMF Section 11.3), not by L×C arithmetic. “Highest consequence wins” when reading the consequence table.

CRITICALNot acceptable. Immediate escalation; stop/contain unless Executive-approved. Documented treatment plan. Board visibility required.
HIGHNot acceptable without treatment. Escalate; documented treatment; active senior oversight until reduced or formally accepted within delegation.
MEDIUMAcceptable within managed operations. Controls + monitoring; treat where weak, deteriorating or above target.
LOWAcceptable within routine operations. Standard controls; routine monitoring; escalate only if profile changes.

2UnlikelyCould occur but is not expectedOnce every 5–10 years5–20%
1RareOnly in exceptional circumstancesLess than once in 10 years<5%

Consequence Scale — RMF Appendix A

Read across the row for each domain and pick the worst level. The highest consequence wins. Financial bands are draft values to be calibrated to NRAR’s operating budget.

Data / informationMinor data errorLocalised quality issueLoss of confidence in a datasetLoss / breach of important dataLoss / breach of critical regulatory data or evidence
Service delivery / operationalNegligible disruptionMinor delayNoticeable disruptionMajor disruption to core functionsCore regulatory functions cannot operate

Control Effectiveness — RMF Appendix D

Control effectiveness is assessed across design (would it work if operated as intended?) and implementation (is it actually operating, with evidence?). The combination produces a six-level overall rating using the Design × Implementation matrix below. Only Effective or Substantially Effective controls justify a residual reduction; lower ratings indicate a control gap.

EffectiveVery strong design AND very strong/strong implementation. Controls consistently operating as intended.
Substantially EffectiveStrong design with strong or adequate implementation. Mature and unlikely to fail significantly.
Partially EffectiveAdequate design but limited or inconsistent implementation. Failures have occurred or are expected.
LimitedLimited design — reduces some aspects of risk but likely to fail. Heavy reliance on manual workarounds.
WeakPoor design even when used correctly. Little or no protection. Only addresses part of the risk.
IneffectiveConsistently not operating as intended. Rates of failure are significant and unacceptable.

RMF Risk Categories

10 official categories · May 2026 · Used in all register dropdowns

12 RMF categories · used in all register dropdowns and reports. Innovation/change is treated as an opportunity lens across all twelve.

#CategoryDescription
1Regulatory effectiveness & outcomesWhether NRAR detects, prioritises and responds to the right risks and achieves its regulatory outcomes.
2Regulated entity behaviour & complianceThe behaviour and compliance capability of water users, and NRAR’s influence over it.
3Enforcement & statutory decision-makingThe lawfulness, consistency, proportionality and defensibility of enforcement and statutory decisions.
4Environmental, catchment & cultural outcomesHarm to water resources, catchments, communities and Aboriginal cultural values.
5Public trust, fairness & reputationPublic confidence in NRAR’s fairness, competence, transparency and independence.
6Independence & integrityRegulatory capture, conflicts of interest, bias, fraud, corruption and misconduct.
7Legal, regulatory & government complianceCompliance with legislation, delegations, government policy and Treasury requirements.
8Data, information & intelligenceThe quality, integrity, security, availability and governance of data, information and evidence.
9Work health, safety & wellbeingPhysical and psychological health and safety of staff, contractors and others affected by NRAR’s work.
10Workforce & capabilityCapability, capacity, conduct and stability of the workforce.
11Operations, continuity & deliveryReliable delivery of strategy and core operations, including business continuity, process and physical sites.
12Financial sustainability & value for moneyFinancial management, procurement, fraud prevention and value for money.
Note: Enterprise-wide risks may exist in more than one category. The primary category should reflect the dominant risk driver.

Risk Category Detail — RMF Appendix G

For each of the 12 categories above, the named risks that commonly sit within it. Click a category to expand. This is reference material to support a risk assessment — it is not an exhaustive list, and a risk may sit across more than one category.

Some risks point to existing external instruments. Two risks below (Cultural values — Category 4, and Artificial intelligence — Category 8) are controlled by adherence to an existing, externally-developed instrument rather than an NRAR-authored process. These are marked with a 🔗 and include what "Effective" means in that context.

Risk Appetite — RMF Section 8 / Risk Appetite Statement

Operating rule (RMF Section 8.3): a risk is within appetite when residual is within tolerance (Medium or below), controls are effective, and residual is at or near its achievable target. A Medium residual with effective controls already at their practical floor is within appetite — even where category appetite is Low — and is monitored, not treated. Where residual cannot be reduced further at proportionate cost, the risk owner may formally informedly accept within delegation, with Executive and (for material risks) Board visibility.

CategoryAppetiteRationale
Regulatory effectiveness & outcomesLow
Aim for Low–Medium residual. Medium acceptable within managed operations. High/Critical not acceptable without treatment.
Opportunity: High — strong appetite to invest in intelligence-led targeting and effectiveness.
Regulated entity behaviour & complianceLow–moderate
Aim for Medium residual. High acceptable with active senior oversight while being treated.
Educate and build voluntary compliance; very low tolerance for unaddressed deliberate, repeated non-compliance.
Enforcement & statutory decision-makingVery low
Aim for Low residual. Medium acceptable only at target with effective controls. High/Critical not acceptable except as documented informed acceptance for irreducible-consequence risks.
Very low tolerance for inconsistent, delayed or poorly evidenced decisions.
Environmental, catchment & cultural outcomesVery low
Aim for Low residual. Medium acceptable only at target with effective controls. High/Critical not acceptable except as documented informed acceptance for irreducible-consequence risks.
Regulatory failure contributing to material environmental or cultural harm is unacceptable.
Public trust, fairness & reputationVery low
Aim for Low residual. Medium acceptable only at target with effective controls. High/Critical not acceptable except as documented informed acceptance for irreducible-consequence risks.
Actions that undermine confidence in NRAR’s fairness and independence are unacceptable.
Independence & integrityVery low
Aim for Low residual. Medium acceptable only at target with effective controls. High/Critical not acceptable except as documented informed acceptance for irreducible-consequence risks.
No tolerance for capture, conflict of interest, bias, fraud or corruption.
Legal, regulatory & government complianceVery low
Aim for Low residual. Medium acceptable only at target with effective controls. High/Critical not acceptable except as documented informed acceptance for irreducible-consequence risks.
No tolerance for failing statutory, government and Treasury obligations.

Aim for Low residual. Medium acceptable only at target with effective controls. High/Critical not acceptable except as documented informed acceptance for irreducible-consequence risks.

Add Risk

Inherent Risk
Inherent risk = likelihood × consequence assuming no controls exist. Score both independently then see the auto-calculated rating.
—
Controls
Residual Risk
Residual risk = likelihood × consequence with current controls in place. Must not exceed the inherent score.
—
Target residual risk  (RMF Section 8.3)

The lowest residual achievable with proportionate, reasonable controls. For safety risks this is the SFAIRP level required by the WHS Act. The residual is judged against this target, not against a fixed number.

—
—

Within appetite when residual is within tolerance (Medium or below) AND controls are effective AND residual is at or near target. Otherwise: treat, or formally accept (informed acceptance) within delegation.

Informed acceptance  (if residual cannot be reduced further at proportionate cost)
NSW AI Assessment Framework (AIAF)  (RMF Appendix G.8 — required for AI systems in development, procurement or use)

NRAR does not run its own AI risk methodology — the control is completion and currency of the AIAF (mandatory under DCS-2024-04). These fields track whether that process has happened; they do not replace the AIAF's own assessment.
